diagnostic_evidence.quote: Therefore, $D\cR (u)$ is invertible with $\| (D\cR (u))^{-1}\| \leq \frac{1}{\mu}$.
By a generalization of Hadamard's theorem by Pourciau \cite{pourciau-82}, this is enough to conclude that $\cR$ is a homeomorphism on $\R^{M+N}$.

issues.failure_explanation: Hadamard's global inverse theorem requires the map to be proper (|R(u)| -> infinity as |u| -> infinity) in addition to having an everywhere invertible Jacobian; invertibility of the Jacobian alone does not imply surjectivity (e.g., exp: R -> R). The proof establishes only ||(DR)^{-1}|| <= 1/mu and never proves properness. The missing step is routine here: every (generalized) Jacobian DR(u) is a mu-diagonally dominant Z-matrix, which yields the expansion |R(u)-R(v)|_inf >= mu|u-v|_inf (mean value theorem in the C^1 case; Clarke's generalized mean value theorem in the Lipschitz case), hence coercivity and properness, after which Hadamard/Pourciau applies.

failure_location.quote: By Hadamard's theorem \cite{hadamard1906transformations}, we deduce that the map $u\conv \cR(u)$ of $\R^{M+N}$ is a diffeomorphism of $\R^{M+N}$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Insert the expansion estimate |R(u)-R(v)|_inf >= mu|u-v|_inf derived from the mu-diagonal dominance of the Z-matrices DR(u) to obtain coercivity/properness before invoking Hadamard (C^1 case) or Pourciau (Lipschitz case).
issues.overall_effect: Part (1) of the theorem (existence and uniqueness of the solution of R(u)=0) rests on an incomplete inference; the statement is true and downstream results (thm:added-1, cor:added-1) remain valid once the missing expansion/properness step is added.
issues.title: Proof of thm:exist-uniqueness-scheme-gen misapplies Hadamard's theorem: properness of R is never established
issues.why_classification: The theorem's statement is true and the gap is filled by a standard short argument; no result, hypothesis, or rate is lost.

issues.failure_explanation: With v = (1-e^{-lambda u})/lambda one has v_t = e^{-lambda u} u_t and grad v = e^{-lambda u} grad u, so v_t + lambda v + ||grad v|| = e^{-lambda u}(u_t + ||grad u||) + lambda v = lambda v, which is nonzero whenever u_t + ||grad u|| = 0. The Kruzhkov transform of a source-free time-dependent equation produces no damping term; the correct equivalence is u_t + ||grad u|| = f(x) iff v_t + ||grad v|| + lambda f(x) v = f(x) (in particular v_t + ||grad v|| = 0 when f = 0). The stationary eikonal equivalence displayed just above (||grad u|| = f iff ||grad v|| + lambda f v = f) is correct, which shows the damping term requires the source f.

issues.failure_explanation: The estimate is false under the stated hypotheses. Counterexample: F(x,u,p) = -a u with a > 0 and a*dt in (0,1) satisfies (F1), (F2) (vacuously, F being independent of p) and (F3) with lambda = a*dt. Take b-bar = c-bar and R(u) = 0 (u solves the scheme exactly). The scheme gives u^{n+1} = u^n/(1-a*dt), hence ||u^{n+1}-v^{n+1}||_inf = ||u^n-v^n||_inf/(1-a*dt) > ||u^n-v^n||_inf, while the claimed right-hand side equals ||u^n-v^n||_inf. The correct comparison is w_j <= z_j + dt*R_j + lambda*w_j, i.e. ||u^{n+1}-v^{n+1}||_inf <= (||u^n-v^n||_inf + dt||R(u)^{n+1}||_inf)/(1-lambda) plus the boundary term. The proof is only the one-line remark 'similar arguments as for the stability of the steady state case', and the recursive bound displayed after the theorem inherits the false non-growth statement (it misses the geometric factor (1-lambda)^{-n}).
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Insert the factor 1/(1-lambda) into the one-step estimate and re-derive the recursion with the resulting geometric growth, or restrict the theorem to F non-decreasing in u (where lambda can be taken arbitrarily small and the stated bound holds).
issues.overall_effect: The stability guarantee for the time-dependent framework is false as stated: errors can grow by the factor 1/(1-lambda) per step even when the residual and boundary data match. The subsequent recursive error estimate is consequently false as well.
issues.title: Time-dependent stability estimate is false (missing 1/(1-lambda) factor); the recursive error bound is also false
issues.why_classification: The advertised non-growth bound is false and the proof is absent, so the statement must be changed; however the repair is contained (one factor) and preserves a recognizably comparable stability estimate with no new proof architecture.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: \mu = \min \left(  \dfrac{\lambda}{M^{1/q}}, \, \left(\dfrac{\mu_b}{N}\right)^{1/q} \right).
Lemma \ref{lem:DR-invertible} shows that the smallest eigenvalue of $D\cR (u)$ is bounded from below by $\sqrt{\Delta x}$.

issues.failure_explanation: The Lemma's bound is mu = min(lambda/M^{1/q}, (mu_b/N)^{1/q}) = O(h^{d/q}) (in the paper's 1D experiments, O(sqrt(dx)), exactly as the numerics section states), not O(h). The sentence 'we derived a lower bound for mu_h to be O(h)' therefore misstates the Lemma; interpreting mu_h as the strong-convexity constant of L = (1/2)||R||^2 gives mu_h = O(h^d) (O(h) in 1D) but then C_h ~ ||DR||^2 = O(h^{d-2}) and kappa_h = O(h^{-2}) in 1D, not O(h^{-1}). The value O(h^{-1}) is the condition number of the Jacobian DR, not of the optimization problem for L, and the iteration counts k ~ (kappa_h/2) log(E_0/tol) built on it are not supported as stated; the quoted rate E_k <= (1-kappa_h^{-1})^{2k} E_0 also omits the standard factor kappa_h.

failure_location.quote: In Lemma~\ref{lem:DR-invertible}, we derived a lower bound for $\mu_h$ to be $O(h)$ so the condition number \n$$\kappa_h := \frac{C_h}{\mu_h} = O(h^{-1}).\n$$

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Recompute the rates consistently: state mu_h = O(h^{d/q}) for sigma_min(DR) (or define mu_h as the strong-convexity constant of L and derive the corresponding C_h and kappa_h), and use the standard gradient-descent bound including the kappa_h factor.
issues.overall_effect: The quantitative rate claims in the warm-start analysis (mu_h, kappa_h, the (1-kappa^{-1})^{2k} rate, and the resulting iteration counts) are unreliable; the qualitative conclusion that warm starting reduces the iteration count is rate-independent and survives.
